quiz.title: Find Your Wellness Style in 8 Everyday Questions
quiz.intro: Eight questions about your ordinary days. Your result names the way your answers lean toward recharging, with one small habit to try this week.

questions.text: After a long week, what helps you feel like yourself again?

options.text: A walk, a swim, or a bike ride
Dinner or a call with people you like
Getting the house and the week ahead in order
A quiet evening with a book or a bath

questions.text: You have a free hour on a weekday. How do you spend it?

options.text: Out the door for some kind of movement
Catching up with a friend or a neighbor
Prepping meals or planning tomorrow
Sitting somewhere quiet with no screen

questions.text: Which small habit would you most like to keep?

options.text: Taking the stairs and a lunchtime walk
Checking in with one person each day
Going to bed and waking at the same time
10 minutes of quiet before the day starts

questions.text: When stress builds up, what do you reach for first?

options.text: Something physical to burn it off
Someone to talk it through with
A list, so the next step is clear
Time alone to slow everything down

questions.text: Pick the weekend plan that sounds best.

options.text: A hike or a game of pickup basketball
A cookout with friends and family
A slow morning, errands done, a tidy home
A long nap and an afternoon in the garden

questions.text: What makes a workday feel balanced?

options.text: Getting up from the desk every hour
A good conversation with a coworker
Finishing on time with tomorrow planned
A real lunch break away from messages

questions.text: Which wellness program would you sign up for?

options.text: A step challenge with a weekly goal
A team volunteer day
A sleep and morning routine series
A guided breathing or quiet-time session

questions.text: What would you tell a friend who feels run down?

options.text: Get outside and move for a bit
Call someone and make plans
Pick one routine and stick with it for a week
Take an evening off and rest

results.title: Mover
results.description: Your answers lean toward recharging through movement: walks, rides, games, anything that gets you out of a chair. Try putting one short walk on the calendar each day, at the same time, and treat it like a meeting.

results.title: Connector
results.description: Your answers lean toward recharging with other people. A good talk or a shared meal resets your week. Try one standing plan each week, such as a Thursday walk or a Sunday call, so time with people does not depend on luck.

results.title: Routine Keeper
results.description: Your answers lean toward recharging through order: a plan for tomorrow, regular hours, a tidy space. Pick one routine to protect this week, such as a set bedtime or a Sunday plan for the week, and keep it for 7 days.

results.title: Quiet Recharger
results.description: Your answers lean toward recharging in quiet: time alone, no screens, a slower pace. Try blocking 20 minutes each day with no messages and nothing to finish, and guard it the way you would guard a meeting.

quiz_plan.promise: the quiz plays the page's promise: a wellness quiz a visitor can take, whose results answer what the H1 says it builds

plan.angle: The top 10 are health publishers and wellness brands offering a quiz to take, with one quiz-maker template page. This page gives both halves: a playable 8-question quiz that names how a person recharges (Mover, Connector, Routine Keeper, or Quiet Recharger), framed as preferences and never as a health score, and four places that act on the result: an employer's open enrollment, a retreat's booking page, a health coach's intake, and a newsletter that plans issues from the counts. Every answer lands in a database the owner keeps.
tab_stories: Quorvale Freight runs the wellness quiz for its 540 employees during open enrollment, and each style's result screen points to the benefit that fits it, so a Connector sees the Thursday lunch walking group.
Duvessa Pimsley takes the quiz on Fenmarsh Retreat's site, lands on Quiet Recharger, and the result page shows the 2-night quiet weekend while the guest coordinator gets an email with her answers.
Coach Ama Brisbeck sends new client Sabeen Kreel 8 questions before their first call, Sabeen answers on her phone as a Routine Keeper, and the answers land in her client record a day ahead.
The Even Keel newsletter counts 2,180 finished quizzes in March, Quiet Recharger leads with 720, and the editor plans April's 4 issues around rest and quiet time.
